idiom_name: HttpServlet subclass mapped to one URL
implementation_notes: The servlet API is the pattern's canonical Java realization: one HttpServlet subclass per page, mapped to its URL by @WebServlet or web.xml, receives the request through doGet/doPost(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse), delegates to domain objects and forwards to a JSP or other view - the container supplies the URL-to-servlet mapping the pattern needs, while shared behaviour lives in filters or a base servlet. Use it with a plain servlet container or when maintaining JSP-era code. Spring MVC is the sibling variant: it keeps the same shape with less ceremony, but adds the framework's already-present front controller, interceptors and dependency injection.
pitfalls: Servlet instances are shared across requests: instance fields are not per-request state, and storing the current user there leaks between users.
URL mapping duplicates the page's identity (@WebServlet or web.xml): renaming a page without updating the mapping breaks the public URL, or silently routes two servlets to one path.
doGet/doPost must not block: holding a container thread on slow I/O or long transactions exhausts the pool - hand off long work explicitly.

variants.name: Spring MVC handler method per page
variants.implementation_notes: Spring MVC's annotation-based model expresses request mapping per method: one @Controller per page area, one @GetMapping/@PostMapping method per page or action, with the DispatcherServlet already acting as the front controller and interceptors or filters carrying shared behaviour. The classic per-page class disappears into a handler method, so prefer this form when Spring already owns routing, dependency injection and view resolution; Spring Framework 6 requires Java 17, which is what makes this a separate variant rather than a style note.
pitfalls: Handler methods live on a singleton controller: never store request state in controller fields.
A @Controller class easily becomes a page bucket - if it holds every page of the site, the per-page locality is gone and you have a front controller with worse structure.
